metadata.title: As AI chip stocks stumble: Why is this analog maker still up 76% in a year?

content.text:
Investing.com and Yahoo Finance LLC may earn commission or revenue on some items through the links below.
Investing.com — The AI chip trade is splitting in two. Worries over soaring data center spending pushed Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ:AMD) down 23.7% in October, and a semiconductor rout after the midterms knocked 7.6% off Texas Instruments (NASDAQ:TXN) on November 5. Yet the analog chipmaker is still up 76.1% over twelve months, helped by 28% revenue growth last quarter.
The gap shows where some investors are turning. Every AI server rack and electric vehicle depends on chips that manage power and signals, and they favor suppliers whose results already prove the demand.
InvestingPro's screening models, which track solvency, margins and cash conversion month after month, keep Texas Instruments in ProPicks AI's Beat the S&P 500 strategy. November's list pairs it with a commercial aerospace propulsion maker, a global digital travel booking leader and a national healthcare insurer, each picked on those same tests.
Find out what made November's large-cap list: Explore the Beat the S&P 500 strategy on InvestingPro
The Analog Supplier Riding the Industrial Recovery
Texas Instruments sells more than 80,000 analog and embedded processing products, and its latest quarter showed how widely demand has turned. Q3 revenue reached $6.06 billion, up 28% from a year earlier and the third straight quarter of beats. Gross margin expanded to 64%, and operating profit hit $2.9 billion, or 47% of revenue. Industrial sales rose more than 40% to a record, data center revenue climbed about 95%, and automotive gained in the mid-teens. Fourth-quarter revenue guidance of $5.8 billion to $6.3 billion came in above analyst expectations.
The cash flow shows the heavy fab-building years starting to pay off. Trailing 12-month free cash flow reached $8.4 billion, against $2.4 billion a year earlier, helped by $1.6 billion in CHIPS Act incentives. The company makes its chips in-house on 300mm wafers, which cut unpackaged chip costs by about 40% versus 200mm, and analysts project free cash flow of $9 to $10 per share in 2027 as capital spending moderates.
What the Numbers Say About the Cycle and the Cash
Investors are paying for that recovery. At $278.10, the stock trades at 35.9 times trailing earnings and 33.9 times 2026 estimates, with a PEG ratio of 0.99. The trailing multiple still sits below the 42.3 times at Analog Devices (NASDAQ:ADI). According to consensus analyst projections compiled on InvestingPro, the average price target is $336.86, about 21% above the current price, and earnings estimates have been revised up seven times over 90 days, with none revised down. InvestingPro's Financial Health framework, which benchmarks companies across more than 100 indicators, scores profitability at 7.8 out of 10, backed by that 64% gross margin.
